en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Girl Vimaladattā, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Yuezhi during the Western Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying on Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa at Rājagṛha together with [the assembly].
Bodhisattvas, great disciples, male novices, female novices, and countless gods, humans, asuras, ghosts, spirits, and dragons were assembled together when the Buddha preached this sutra.

At that time, within the assembly, there was an elder brahmin named Sudāna, who had a wife named Vairocanī. Together with nine hundred and seventy-five billion women, they joined their palms and listened to the sutra.
At that time, Pilu-yen was pregnant; while this girl was within her mother’s womb, her physical form was fully complete, and she even sat with palms joined within the womb listening to the sutra.
The Venerable Aniruddha, by the power of his supernormal vision derived from his own merit, saw this girl with palms joined within the womb listening to the sutra, and he thought to himself:
"Those present in this assembly can see only what their eyes perceive; they are unable to investigate formless matters as I am able."
He then felt fortunate and his countenance became joyful and radiant.
The Buddha asked Ānanda:
"What have you seen that causes your mind and appearance to be so exceptionally joyful?"
Aniruddha said, "With my clairvoyant vision, I saw a girl within the womb joining her palms to listen to the sutra; it was for this reason that I smiled with joy and congratulated myself."
The Buddha said: "Excellent, excellent!
It is just as you have said."
For example, if one were to compare the various stars to the light of the sun and moon, would they ever be equal?

Among the śrāvakas whom you regard as foremost, none can equal you; yet, in the vision of the Tathāgata, all the birds and beasts flying and running throughout the ten directions, as well as the insects within the earth, are seen to be pregnant, and their offspring within the womb are all listening to the sutras exactly as you do.
At that time, Aniruddha and all those in the assembly were filled with doubt.

The Buddha emitted a radiance that shone forth boundlessly; throughout the eight directions, above, and below, there was no obstruction, such that all beings in countless lands could see one another, inside and out, as clearly as looking into a mirror.

Aniruddha and the others looked up into the void and saw flocks of flying birds pausing their wings and hovering about to listen to what the Buddha was saying; even those in the womb of eggs, neither yet hatched nor fully formed, likewise spread their wings within the bird-eggs to listen to the sutra.
Looking down, they saw the four-footed beasts of the wild grazing on grass or drinking from water, who had ceased their activities and stood upright to listen to the sutra;
even those conceived in the womb likewise, while still within the womb, drew up their two front legs and listened to the sutra with single-minded devotion.
Insects, snakes, earthworms, and other creatures born from the earth remained still without moving their bodies, listening to the sutra with focused minds;
among them were those who were pregnant and had not yet given birth, who likewise raised their heads within the womb and coiled their bodies as they listened to the sutra with single-minded devotion.
At that time, Āniruddha, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, addressed the woman in the womb with an eightfold voice:
"O bird, egg, insect, beast, or child in the womb—for what reason do you join your palms, spread your wings, bend your feet, coil your body, and listen to the sutra with single-minded devotion?"
At that time, those women who were pregnant replied to Aniruddha:
"We listen to the sutra because all classes of living beings are deluded by the five sense-bases and do not recognize the Right Path;
we listen to the sutra because all beings are possessed of much lust, anger, and ignorance, and their cycle of birth and death does not cease."
“Because all people are unfilial toward their parents and do not serve the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus, I have permitted this recitation of the sutra.
At that time, Āniruddha, having heard what was said, knelt with his right knee on the ground and addressed the Buddha:

“I recall that the merit, virtue, and penetrating spiritual power of the World-Honored One are such as this; I would rather cast my body into hell to endure manifold bitter sufferings for countless kalpas than attain arhatship.”

Why is this? Those who are still within the womb and have not yet seen their own bodies can still give rise to the great resolve to save all beings; yet I now use my body out of fear of death, bound by perceptions and consciousness, like a dead man who can no longer benefit others.

At that moment, the girl was born, emerging from her mother’s right side. The three thousandfold world-system shook violently. Countless devas dwelling in the void rained down celestial flowers and played various musical instruments; there then appeared natural thousand-petaled lotuses, as large as chariot wheels, with stalks like lapis lazuli, upon which the girl sat.

At that time, all the devas, humans, birds, beasts, insects, snakes, earthworms, and those who were pregnant likewise gave birth. It was like when a king goes on a military expedition; none of his officials, whether great or small, fail to follow him.
Thereupon, the Lord of Devas took a celestial robe and descended from above to give it to the woman. Her naked form was loathsome, so she took this robe and put it on.
The sons of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven and the various princesses also took robes and gave them to all the sentient beings.
Then the woman replied:
"As for those who have not yet escaped the mire of desire and nirvana, we do not receive anything from them.
You are an Arhat, while my aspiration lies with the Bodhisattvas; you are not of my kind, for our vows are different."
The Lord of Devas spoke again:
"Because my female body is naked and loathsome, I have taken this garment to give to you.
The woman replied once more:
“In the Mahāyāna Dharma, there is neither male nor female; I shall now have natural robes appear spontaneously.
The Buddha said to Śakra, Lord of Devas:

“In this way, one does not adorn a woman’s body; rather, by generating the bodhicitta, one naturally attains the marks and signs of excellence. It is the manifestation of these infinite qualities that constitutes the true adornment of a bodhisattva’s body.”
At that time, Śāriputra was deeply astonished that this girl had undergone such a transformation;
he stepped forward and said to the Buddha, “From which country has this girl come to this place? Who sent her these robes?”
The Buddha said:

"This woman has come from the presence of the Buddha Dharmasvabhāva in the land of Pūrvavideha in the southeast. Her realm is named Jambūnada, situated one hundred thousand Buddha-fields away from here. This woman came from her own country desiring to see the Buddha; she naturally brought clothing with her from her own country."
The robe then spontaneously appeared in mid-air with a rustling sound, and a voice from the sky spoke to the girl, saying:
"You may wear this robe; you shall obtain the five supernatural powers."

Furthermore, all the women of her native land had attained the five supernormal powers (*pañcābhijñā*). When the woman received the robes, she descended from the flower to the place where the Buddha was. As soon as she lifted one foot, heaven and earth shook in six ways. All the women conceived the aspiration for supreme, equal enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). Among the flying birds and beasts, there were none who did not turn back their forms and transform into humans, their bodies clad in celestial garments, pearl necklaces, and ornaments.
The woman bowed her head to the Buddha’s feet in prostration, three times uttered "Namo Samyaksambuddha," and knelt with her right knee on the ground, saying to the Buddha:
"I pray that you will extensively expound the Dharma for all those gathered here, so that they may attain their aspirations."
The Buddha, in accordance with their wishes, immediately preached the sutra for them.

At that time, this woman and nine hundred and seventy-five billion mothers, having heard what the Buddha taught, leaped for joy and were no longer reborn as women; they stood before the Buddha and were transformed into men, each removing their necklaces and precious jewels to scatter over the Buddha.

Through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, that which was scattered was spontaneously transformed into a jeweled canopy with interlacing pendants. Within it was a lion throne made of the seven treasures, upon which sat a Buddha who raised his hand and praised them; at that moment, they all attained the stage of *avaivartika*.

Even birds, beasts, insects, and snakes who have attained human form likewise cast off their pearl necklaces and precious ornaments to scatter them over the Buddha as he sits within the pavilion; these offerings coalesce to form a jeweled canopy, exactly as before and without any difference, which constitutes a *dakṣiṇā*, and all attain the seventh stage.
The Buddha addressed the female bodhisattva, the virtuous woman Vimalā:

"Just as you act as a guide for sentient beings while within the womb, so too does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, act as a guide for all sentient beings throughout the five realms of existence."
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the entire assembly was filled with great joy; they prostrated themselves and withdrew.
Thus ends the *Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Girl Vimaladatta*.
